First Love
FURST luhv
noun (spiritual condition)
From the charge to the church at Ephesus, "thou hast left thy first love" (Rev 2:4); first denoting the earliest and warmest devotion of the new convert.

📖 Biblical Definition

"First love" is the phrase Christ uses in His letter to the church at Ephesus: "Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love" (Rev 2:4). The Ephesian church was, by every outward measure, exemplary. Christ commends its works, its labor, its patience, its hatred of evil men, its testing and exposing of false apostles, its endurance for His name's sake without fainting (Rev 2:2-3). It was sound in doctrine and tireless in labor. Yet the searching eye of the Lord found a fatal cooling beneath the diligence: the ardent love that marked its beginning had grown cold. Orthodoxy and industry had outlasted affection. This is a sobering word, that a church may contend rightly for the truth and toil without ceasing, and still grieve its Lord by losing the first warmth of love to Him. The remedy Christ gives is threefold and exact: "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works" (Rev 2:5) — remember the height from which the heart has slipped, repent of the cooling, and return to the deeds love first prompted. The warning is grave: else "I will remove thy candlestick out of his place." This dictionary confesses that sound doctrine and busy hands cannot substitute for love to Christ, and that the cooled heart is recovered by remembrance, repentance, and a return to first works.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The warm devotion of the Ephesian church which it had left, though sound in doctrine and labor (Rev 2:4). The threefold remedy: remember, repent, and do the first works.

expand to see more

FIRST LOVE, noun. The earliest, ardent devotion to Christ which the Ephesian church had abandoned while remaining busy and orthodox.

Christ commended its labor and patience yet charged it with cooled affection.

"Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love" (Rev 2:4).

Sound doctrine and tireless works cannot replace love to Christ.

The remedy: "remember... and repent, and do the first works" (Rev 2:5).

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 2:4 — "Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love."

Rev 2:5 — "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent."

Rev 2:2 — "I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars:"

Matt 24:12 — "And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

First love faces no postmodern redefinition; the principle to recover is the warning that sound doctrine and labor cannot replace warm love to Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The Ephesian danger is the peculiar peril of the orthodox: that a church zealous for truth, diligent in works, and discerning of error may yet let its love to Christ grow cold. The very strengths Christ commends — labor, patience, doctrinal vigilance — can mask a cooling heart, for they continue by habit and conviction even as affection wanes. "The love of many shall wax cold" (Matt 24:12) is fulfilled not only in apostates but in the dutiful.

The principle to recover is that Christ wants the heart, not merely the hands. He will not be content with a sound creed and a busy calendar if the warmth of love is gone. The remedy is not less doctrine or less labor, but love restored to govern both: "remember... and repent, and do the first works" (Rev 2:5). This dictionary confesses that the chief commandment is to love the Lord with all the heart (Matt 22:37), and that the cure for a cooled church is to return, in remembrance and repentance, to the deeds that flowed from its first love.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The phrase recalls the new convert's earliest and warmest devotion to Christ, which the Ephesians had let cool though their works continued.

expand to see more

First, the earliest, the devotion of the beginning.

Love here is ardent affection toward Christ Himself.

Ephesus kept the works but left the warmth that bore them.

Christ counts the cooling a fall to be repented of.

The first works flow again from love restored.

Usage

"A church may keep sound doctrine and yet leave its first love."

"Christ's remedy for lost first love is to remember, repent, and do the first works."

"First love is recovered not by more labor but by warmed affection to Christ."
